goal: Reconcile county socioeconomic trends with CDC PLACES health outcomes. Download three USDA ERS county files (education, population components 2020-23, unemployment/income), build a normalized SQLite DB with an exclusions table, an Excel workbook (tercile ANOVA matrix, Blinder-Oaxaca metro decomposition, outlier sheet), and a notebook fitting static vs dynamic models with LR/IC comparison, state-level Moran's I, poverty-inactivity-obesity mediation and figures. Finish with a 2-3 page memo.
delivered: county_analysis.db (identifiers, socioeconomic_current/historical, health_outcomes, demographic_dynamics, exclusions, FIPS indexes), disparity_profile.xlsx (Change-by-Health Matrix, Metro Decomposition, Outlier Flag Sheet), reconciliation_models.ipynb, and reconciliation_memo.pdf with three embedded figures. All three USDA files were obtained and pivoted from long format; the tercile ANOVA and snapshot/change tables passed.
what_went_wrong: Models entered RUCC as one numeric slope with no justification, never checked multicollinearity (no correlation matrix or VIF) among four highly correlated SES predictors, and reported only n/AIC/BIC/LR, with no coefficient, SE, p-value or R-squared tables. The memo gave no count or pattern for flagged outlier counties and no recommendations, and Moran's I was reported without E[I]. demographic_dynamics used self-computed 2020-23 period rates and percent change instead of the file's R_NET_MIG_2023/R_NATURAL_CHG_2023 and absolute change, and economic typology came from the 2025 Industry_Dependence codes rather than Economic_typology_2015. The prompt does not specify either choice.

failed_items.why: The prompt asks for 'net migration rate, natural change rate, population change for 2020-2023'. The agent stored net_migration_rate_2020_23, natural_change_rate_2020_23 and population_change_pct_2020_23 (period rates per 1,000 of mean population), which is a reasonable reading. The rubric requires the single-year R_NET_MIG_2023/R_NATURAL_CHG_2023 and absolute change, a choice the prompt does not imply. The exclusions table and indexes passed.

State-averaged residuals, queen weights with isolates and Moran's I with a 999-permutation p-value were all done, but moran() returns only I, p and n. The null expectation E[I] = -1/(n-1), a standard part of reporting Moran's I, appears nowhere.

The prompt explicitly asks for 'patterns among flagged outlier counties'. The memo's outlier paragraph (page 3) only points to the Excel sheet, with no flag count and no observed clusters (e.g. WV/TN depression outliers visible in the sheet). Limitations cover ecological inference and temporal alignment but give no next-step recommendations.

The notebook uses rucc_2023 as one numeric slope (no dummies or justification, although the memo calls it categorical). It has no .corr() or VIF for poverty, income, unemployment and education, and prints only n/AIC/BIC/LR rather than coefficient, SE, p and R-squared tables.

Long-format pivoting was correct for all four ERS files, and the downloaded population.csv did contain R_NET_MIG_2023, R_NATURAL_CHG_2023 and Economic_typology_2015. The agent instead derived 2020-23 component rates and used 2025 County Typology Industry_Dependence; the prompt names neither the rate year nor the typology edition, so the rubric's exact attribute list is not implied.

subagent_notes: Three subagents: 'Research USDA county datasets' located the ERS URLs (its web_fetch calls hit the 5 MB limit and an unsupported xlsx content type, but root then downloaded the CSVs to data_downloads/), 'Plan statistical analysis' proposed methods, and 'Find existing reference artifacts' profiled the staged CSVs. They helped data retrieval and planning. The methods plan specified 'RUCC dummies' as controls and noted multicollinearity concerns, but root coded rucc_2023 as numeric and never ran VIF, so that advice was not used (R6). No failure was caused by a subagent.
